answer: We formulate a mechanism comprising dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices, wherein agents deposit collateral into a vault, facing penalty for Sybilization. As agents weigh benefits against ember of potential losses, capital barrier analysis reveals expected payoff of identity multiplication is strictly negative. Consequently, in adversarial multi-agent environments, strategic interaction converges to Nash equilibrium, where no agent can improve payoff by unilaterally deviating, even on treacherous terrain of a shifting dune.
